entries.not_relevant_because: The manuscript settles Wall's finite D(2) problem: it builds a finite connected 3-dimensional complex X with infinite fundamental group that satisfies the D(2) homology conditions but is not homotopy equivalent to any finite complex of dimension at most two. The question concerns finite complexes and their finite 2-dimensional homotopy models. The Eilenberg-Ganea conjecture concerns groups G with integral cohomological dimension 2 and asks for a 2-dimensional K(G,1). Neither the abstract, the introduction, the tower or plus-construction sections, nor the construction section mentions cohomological dimension of a group, K(G,1), asphericity, geometric dimension, or Eilenberg-Ganea (checked by keyword search over all the manuscript's sources). The manuscript does not claim that pi_1(X) has cohomological dimension 2, and it does not claim that any group of cohomological dimension 2 lacks a 2-dimensional aspherical model. The matching pass's link is a shared theme of Wall-type dimension questions, not an overlap of the stated problems.
